title: Flare Tier - Surge Credits & On-demand QoS (scratchpad)
content:
Goal: sketch a compact, sellable 'Flare' add-on that lets customers buy short-lived QoS/throughput boosts (surge credits) when latency or throughput matters. Keep it simple enough for product to ship quickly, but with clear unit-econ and guardrails for infra teams.

High-level idea
- Flare = purchased credit balance that can be applied to requests to (a) increase scheduling priority, (b) bump to reserved burst pool (higher throughput), and/or (c) force a lower-latency execution path (smaller batch windows, prewarmed kernels).
- Billing primitives: credits (units) consumed per request or per-minute of boosted capacity. Credits convert to USD.
- UX: checkbox in Console / header in API call: {flare:true, flare_profile:"p0"}. If credit balance insufficient, request falls back to best-effort (or fails if customer opts-in strict).

Two charging models to experiment with
A) Per-request credit multiplier: each request tagged FLARE multiplies base token charge by X (e.g., 2x or 3x). Simple mapping to existing invoicing.
B) Time-window reservation: customer burns credits to reserve N GPU-minutes of burst capacity in a region for M minutes. More predictable for SRE capacity planning.

Quick unit-econ assumptions (back-of-envelope) — baseline infra costs
- Assumed committed GPU cost (amortized): $3.50 / GPU-hour (post-discount/hybrid reserved estimate for production).
- Approx throughputs (tokens/sec) on representative models (quantized, serving runtime):
  - 7B -> 1,500 t/s (tokens per second)
  - 13B -> 900 t/s
  - 70B -> 250 t/s
Notes: these are coarse; actual numbers depend on kv-cache, seq len, and batching. Use median for econ.

Derived figures
- tokens/hour = t/s * 3600
  - 7B: 1,500 * 3600 = 5,400,000 tokens/hour
  - 13B: 900 * 3600 = 3,240,000 tokens/hour
  - 70B: 250 * 3600 = 900,000 tokens/hour
- cost per 1M tokens = ($3.50 / tokens/hour) * 1,000,000
  - 7B: $3.50 / 5.4 = $0.648 ~ $0.65 / 1M tokens
  - 13B: $3.50 / 3.24 = $1.08 / 1M tokens
  - 70B: $3.50 / 0.9 = $3.89 / 1M tokens

Interpretation
- If hosted base price for generation is e.g. $0.60 / 1M (target entry-level), then 7B is near break-even for raw GPU cost; 13B gives some margin; 70B is expensive to serve. Flare pricing should reflect incremental marginal cost (extra kernel warmups, smaller batching -> lower throughput) and a willingness-to-pay for latency.

Flare pricing primitives (first draft)
1) Flare multiplier (simple): charge = base_token_price * flare_multiplier. Default multiplier candidates: 2x (conservative), 3x (strict latency), 5x (exclusive burst).
   - Pros: easy integration; invoice lines simple.
   - Cons: doesn't map cleanly to actual GPU minutes consumed for large models.

2) Flare credit -> GPU-minute mapping (recommended for Dedicated + Private):
   - Define 1 flare-credit = 1 GPU-minute of reserved burst capacity (region + model family). Price per credit = GPU-hour-price / 60 * surcharge. E.g., GPU-hour $3.50 -> $0.0583 / GPU-minute. Add infra surcharge (maintenance, priority switching) -> round to $0.08/credit.
   - For 13B: 1 GPU-minute yields ~900 t/s * 60 = 54,000 tokens/min = 3.24M tokens/hour (consistent). So cost per 1M tokens while using Flare-reserved capacity ~ $0.08 * (1M / 54k) = $1.48 / 1M tokens (includes surcharge).

Pricing scenarios (sample)
- Customer A (chat app) occasional spikes: wants 1 minute bursts to keep UX snappy on heavy flows. If they buy a 1k-credit pack at $0.08/credit = $80, that's 1000 GPU-min = ~16.7 GPU-hours of burst. If they use that on 13B profile, tokens served ~16.7 * 3.24M = 54M tokens. Effective cost = $80 / 54M = $1.48 / 1M tokens (matches mapping).
- Customer B (low-latency RL loop) requires strict p0 priority; we recommend multiplier x3 on base token price (simpler) + a minimum monthly commit for reserved hot pool.

Design constraints and guardrails
- Minimum burn window: avoid tiny 1-second bursts that are SRE nightmares. Enforce min 15s or 1 minute billing granularity.
- Backpressure: if dedicated burst pool exhausted, fall back to base queue (flag in response). Possible SLA: percentage of flare requests guaranteed within latency X while capacity remains.
- Anti-abuse: rate-limit per-account flare toggles to prevent constant churning. Add cooldown (e.g., 10s) on successive flare toggles.
- Visibility: Console show "flare budget remaining", per-route flare usage, and cost rundown. Alerts when low.

Simplified API surface (proto)
- header: x-redwood-flare: {profile:p0|p1|p2, mode:multiplier|reserve, credits_requested: N}
- response: flare_status:{applied:true|false, reason:queue|insufficient_credits, consumed_credits:N}

Open questions / TODOs
- How to represent multi-tenant fairness when multiple customers hold flare credits in same region? (SRE needs reservations or true preemption?)
- Pricing elasticity tests: what multiplier/window customers will accept? quick A/B ideas: 2x at $0.5/1M -> is conversion ok?
- Attribution: should flare consumption be shown on per-request logs and correlate with SLO metrics? (yes, for billing disputes)
- Should we allow auto-topup of credits with a soft cap? (UX improvement)
- Edge case: streaming responses where flare applies to initial tokens only vs whole stream — define policy.

Operational notes for infra team
- Implement tagging in scheduler so flare requests get smaller batch thresholds and prewarmed kernels where feasible.
- Telemetry: sample trace + flare flag to measure actual throughput delta; collect 95p latency for flare vs non-flare across model families.
- Rollout plan: start with multiplier mode for hosted (fast), pilot credit-reserve for Dedicated customers.

Action items
- [ ] Run 3 controlled perf runs on serving runtime: 7B/13B/70B with 1) small-batches+prewarm, 2) default batching. Capture tokens/sec and 95p latency. (Owner: Diego)
- [ ] Pricing experiments: create two A/Bs in Console: (A) multiplier 2x, (B) credits priced at $0.08/credit with 1k pack discount. Measure take-rate. (Owner: Priya)
- [ ] UX mock for Console + API headers + billing line. (Owner: Alex)

Notes-to-self: keep Flare messaging simple: "Buy burst credits for guaranteed priority and lower latency — consumed when you opt-in per-request." Avoid too many knobs in first launch.

Patchy/unfinished thoughts (brain-dump)
- Might want a 'soft' flare that only affects batch window, and 'hard' flare that preempts queued jobs. Different pricing buckets.
- Consider 'auto-flare' where we auto-apply credits when detected latency > threshold; charges via credit balance with opt-out. Careful with surprise billing.
- For Private customers, map credits to specific on-prem nodes (helps SRE limit scope).

End of scratchpad.
